doc.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Alumni All-Stars: tuba, founding and early members
summary: No bass or tuba in the Catatonic Five; the All-Stars began in the early fifties when Paul Parker recruited him, with sons Mike and Larry, John VonBergen, Emerson and Collier.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Did you have a bass player in the group?
Not in the Catatonic Five we didn’t.
We just got our tuba in recent years and that was not the Catatonic Five, it’s the Alumni All-Stars, which is the band closest to my heart.
And Gordy is a wonderful tuba player. He goes to tuba camp you know, to learn jazz. Jazz tuba camp.
That’s cool. Now the Alumni All-Stars, is there an official first year of their existence?

I don’t think there’s a definitive year. It’s the early fifties. I was the first drummer in the Alumni All-Stars because Paul Parker needed a drummer and he asked me. I was in the Catatonic Five. So he knew I was a drummer. And he said, “Come on, we’re going to play the same kind of music.” And he had his son, Mike Parker, playing cornet, and another son, Larry, playing bass. And then we were joined by John VonBergen, remember John?
So we had a bass player. When Larry left we had John VonBergen. And then I got Emerson Brown and then we got Collier and we had a Dixieland band.
